question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund (Cat III) is evaluating a peer-group benchmark drawn from a commercial hedge-fund index that only includes funds currently reporting. The portfolio-construction team at the fund's investment committee flags a specific bias that inflates the benchmark's average return. Which bias is this?

answer.text: Self-reporting bias — only well-performing funds volunteer data
Strategy heterogeneity — funds with different mandates are pooled together
Backfill bias — new funds add historical returns selectively on joining the index
Survivorship bias — funds that closed, liquidated, or stopped reporting are excluded from the index history

explanation.text: The Logic: Survivorship bias is the index-construction effect in which funds that liquidated, merged, or stopped reporting (often due to poor performance) are dropped from the historical series, leaving a "survivor" set whose average return is upward-biased. The stem describes exactly this mechanism — an index that only includes funds currently reporting. It is distinct from self-reporting bias (voluntary-reporting skew) and backfill bias (selective backdating of joiner history). The Trap: Options A (self-reporting) and C (backfill) describe real but different biases. Option B (strategy heterogeneity) is a peer-construction issue, not an index-bias mechanism. Note: Survivorship, self-reporting, backfill, and commercial hedge-fund index-bias mechanics are not explicitly set out in the cited XIX-E (Category III AIF Managers) workbook pages, which support hedge-fund/Cat III strategy diversity and benchmarking-challenge concepts generally. The framing reflects general industry knowledge of hedge-fund index construction.
